# W2-137 (DAEO-5emz): the independent review, round 1

Reviewer: independent-auditor, a fresh read-only session, 2026-11-07. Branch `w2/W2-137` at `f01d51a4e`, against
`w2/integrate` (`git diff w2/integrate...w2/W2-137`, 22 files). Judged under `governance/project/briefs/JUDGEMENT.md`
(ADR-0001's threat model; the two questions on every finding).

## Step 0 and the process check
- Sandbox check: (a) the write to `/home/usain/gov-os-worktrees/.sandbox-trial-W2-137` failed (`OSError: [Errno 30]
  Read-only file system`); (b) `git hash-object -w --stdin` gave `1ae28402a109…` and `git update-index --refresh` worked.
- `ps -eo pid,args | grep -iE "[o]llama|[l]lama-server"`: nothing.

## What I ran (read-only, through the heavy slot, HOME an empty scratch folder, no GPU, no model)
- `tests/acceptance/W2-137`, `tests/unit/retrieval/test_w2_137_request_cap.py`, `test_w2_32_whole_chunk.py`,
  `test_w2_32_routing.py`, `test_w2_32_pool.py`, with `-m "not local_only" -k "not real and not green_here and not
  time_limit"`: **123 passed, 70 deselected** (9 min 52 s, mostly the slot's wait).
- The D-2 files, `tests/acceptance/W2-32/test_w2_32_s7_dec1067.py`, `…s7_size_bound.py`, `…s8_routing.py`,
  `…s8_phrasings.py`, `…s11_pool.py`, `tests/acceptance/W1-19/test_w1_19_semantic_index.py`, plus
  `tests/acceptance/W1-21/test_w1_21_merge.py`, with the same exclusion: **95 passed, 9 deselected, 1 xfailed** (99 s).
- Left out by the exclusion: the real-model, `local_only`, `green_here` and `time_limit` rows (the CTO's, outside the
  sandbox). I did not run `test_w2_112_shared_reranker.py` (the sandbox refuses its Unix socket). I rely on the CTO's
  85 passed for those cases and its 943/1 scoped run, and I read the two revised W2-112 assertions myself.

## The change, read
- `rerank.py`: `MAX_REQUEST_TEXTS` 16 → 64; `MAX_REQUEST_CHARS` (24,000) and `requests()` unchanged; the docstring
  updated. `requests()` takes the longest text first and `fits = min(cap, 24_000 // longest)`, so the padded bound
  limits every request whatever the cap is.
- `rerank_service.py`: `MAX_TEXTS` stays 512 (≥ 64); a request over it now has its own `ValueError` naming the bound
  and the count ("…at most 512 texts: this one has 513, none scored") and is checked before `scores` is called. A
  malformed request keeps the old reason. `serve()`/`released()` are untouched, so the release and the `MEMORY` line
  still follow every request that was read, whether it scored or failed.

## Per KPI line

**S1, pass.** 40 short texts go in one request: unit `test_s1_short_texts_at_the_pool_s_depth_go_in_one_request[40|60]`,
`test_s1_a_rerank_of_40_short_candidates_asks_the_shared_service_once` (one `_ask` of 40), and the designer's
`test_s1_the_pool_s_short_texts_go_in_one_request[…]` up to 40 × 552 (padded exactly 24,000). The padded bound still
splits long texts: 40 × 2,000 goes as 11/11/11/7, 40 × 1,000 as 22/18, and a 23,000-character text goes alone with the
39 short ones in one request. A text over the bound is cut to fit it. The randomised mixed pools (1 to 200 texts,
1 to 26,000 characters) keep both bounds and send each text once. The designer's self-check (cap 64 passes all 37, a
broken bound fails 21) shows the cases can fail.

**S2, pass.** `MAX_TEXTS` 512 ≥ 64, guarded by `test_s2_the_service_s_bound_is_at_least_the_client_s_cap` and the
designer's twin. A request of 513 is refused whole: no `scores` key, and the encoder is never called (`encoder.calls ==
[]`). The reason names the bound and the count. The client raises "the service refused the request: …" with the reason
in it, and the default scorer then falls back with the reason in its FALLBACK line. An answer one score short is an
error, never a cut. A reranker that drops texts leaves the pool unscored with `unavailable` and the count named.

**S3, pass (as a unit property).** `rerank()` writes each score back at its candidate's index, so how the texts are
split cannot change the order. The engineer's cases (40/60/100 short, 10 long + 30 short, 1 huge + 39 short) and the
designer's (a stand-in encoder whose scores move by less than 1e-5 with the batch's padding) give the same order and a
largest difference within 1e-3. The service-level case compares one request of 40 with requests of 16 directly. The
live check is S5's (see the GPU section for its risk).

**S4, pass.** For requests of 1, 16, 40, 64, 512 and 513 texts, `serve` releases exactly once, after the answer (or the
refusal) is sent, and writes exactly one `MEMORY` line with allocated and reserved MiB. A search's requests each
release once. Only W2-112's two cap-pinning assertions changed (`== 16` → `== 64`; the tuple `(16, 24_000, 512)` →
`(64, 24_000, 512)`); the other W2-112 tests are as they were (CTO: 85 passed outside the sandbox).

**D-2, pass.** Every revised case carries `Rewrite-Reason: DEC-1090 (2)`. The cap is now read from the code that runs
(`rerank.MAX_REQUEST_TEXTS`, and in W1-19 through a child process of the same `gov` the driver runs; W2-32's driver
uses the same `GOV_SRC` the test imports). Each case also gained a new check, at most `rerank_service.MAX_TEXTS`, and
24,000 padded characters stays a literal. Case by case:
- `s7_size_bound`: both bounds, the fewest requests (`_fewest` reads the cap in force), the order unbatched, and the
  40,000-character text cut. Kept whole.
- `s8_phrasings` and `s8_routing`: the premise "the pool is over 16" keeps the literal 16 (`DEC_1067_CAP`), so the
  fixture is still one the old cap would have split. "One rerank of the merged pool" is still checked: `_fewest(pool)`
  is now 1 request, and `all(size == CAP for size in sizes[:-1])` fails two passes of their own (e.g. [10, 10]). If
  anything this is stricter than before.
- `W1-19`: "every request full but the last" became "as few requests as both bounds allow" plus "grouped once, longest
  first" (each request's shortest text is no shorter than the next request's longest). `_fewest` matches `requests()`
  step for step. R2-F3's purpose, catching two passes of their own that interleave lengths, is kept. The check is the
  right shape now that the padded bound, not the count, splits this set (19 and 10).
- `s11_pool` / `w2_32_pool.within_bound`: the docstring and the cap read from the code; the 24,000 bound is unchanged.
No expectation was lowered: every literal 16 that bounded a request became the cap in force plus the service's bound,
and the 16s that remain are premises only.

## Memory on the GPU (for S5's window)

How a request is scored (read from the reranker environment, `sentence_transformers` 6.1.0, `transformers` 5.18.0,
`torch` 2.14.1; Qwen3-Reranker-0.6B, `torch_dtype` bfloat16):
- `CrossEncoder.predict` sorts the pairs longest first and runs batches of 32. Each batch is padded to its own
  longest. The text-generation task gets no flattening.
- The model computes logits for the last token only (`logits_to_keep = 1`, then `LogitScore`), so there is no
  full-vocabulary tensor per position. A forward pass's memory grows with its batch × padded tokens.

**The peak stays bounded.** A request of n texts with n × longest ≤ 24,000:
- Its first predict batch holds min(32, n) of its longest texts, so that batch's padded characters are at most
  min(32, n) × longest ≤ 24,000. No forward pass is larger, in counted characters, than the single forward pass of a
  full request under the old cap.
- A request of 40 is two forward passes (32 + 8), and one of 64 is 32 + 32. The caching allocator reuses blocks
  between them, and `empty_cache` runs after the request.
- So the larger request's peak is about one full forward pass plus some fragmentation, not four times the old one.

**One risk for S5's window: the per-pair prompt is not counted.**
- The chat template (`chat_template.jinja`: the system line, `<Instruct>`, `<Query>`, `<Document>`, the
  `<think></think>` tail) adds about 350 characters, roughly 80 tokens, to every pair. `rerank.py`'s comment says
  "about 80 characters a pair", but it is about 80 *tokens*.
- That margin scales with the pairs in one forward pass, which can now be 32 rather than 16. Worst case: 32 pairs of
  about 750 characters ≈ 32 × (190 + 80) ≈ 8,600 tokens, against 16 × (375 + 80) ≈ 7,300 under the old cap. That is
  about 18 % more tokens in the largest forward pass.
- On a 0.6B model with SDPA attention this is tens to a few hundred MiB above the 1,168 MiB the model holds, far
  inside the 3.5 GB share and the 14,255 MiB budget. It is still a rise S5 should see rather than assume.
- W2-112's memory-release acceptance case still sends "a full request" as 16 texts of about 1,478 characters. S5's
  peak sampling should include requests of 32 to 64 texts at the padded bound (e.g. 32 × ~700 and 64 × ~330
  characters).

**A second risk for S5: the 1e-3 tolerance live.** The model runs in bfloat16, and its score is the raw yes/no logit
difference (identity activation). With the pool's 40 in one request, each text lands in a different predict batch with
different padding than under requests of 16. In bfloat16 that can move a raw logit by around 1e-2, more than S3's
1e-3, and can swap near-ties. This is not new: under the old cap, a text's batch already depended on its neighbours.
But if the CTO checks "largest difference within 1e-3" live, it may fail on rounding alone. S5's stated measure (hit@5
and MRR within 1, the order on the same candidates) is the robust one.

**Queueing.** It is unchanged in total work: 20 requests of 40 instead of 60 of up to 16. The client's 30 s read
timeout covers queue time, as before.

## Findings (each one a row; none blocks)

**F1 (D-2, out of this round's paths): W1-21's `RERANK_CAP = 16` was not revised.** D-2's settled list names it.
`tests/acceptance/W1-21/test_w1_21_merge.py:17` still says `RERANK_CAP = 16`, with `len(sizes) == ceil(n/16)` and
"every request full but the last". It passes today only because W1-21's merged sets are at most 16 texts (the
engineer's evidence agrees). If a W1-21 fixture grows past 16, the case turns red against correct code.
- Ordinary work: yes, because a test designer who adds notes to W1-21's fixture meets it with no warning.
- Consequence: other (a false red, which fails closed; nothing passes that should not).
- Scope: out (D-2's revision is the designer's, and W1-21 is not in this ticket's paths). Rather than fail D-2: a row,
  or revise it as D-2 said, the next time W1-21's tests are touched.

**F2: test names still say "16".** These now assert 64 or the cap in force:
- unit `test_no_request_to_the_reranker_carries_more_than_16_texts`, `test_the_shared_service_is_asked_at_most_16_texts_at_a_time`,
  `test_routing_on_keeps_one_rerank_of_the_merged_set_in_full_requests_of_16`, `test_no_request_is_above_16_texts_or_24000_…`;
- acceptance `…_more_than_16_texts_…`, `…_within_16_texts_…`, `test_the_16_text_cap_holds_with_routing_on`.
The acceptance names were kept on purpose (the README node ids), and the file docstrings say so.
- Ordinary work: yes, because a reader takes the name for the bound.
- Consequence: other (misleading names, no behaviour).
- Scope: in. A row.

**F3: end-to-end coverage of splitting by count is narrower.** At pools of 20 to 31, `s7_dec1067`, `s8_routing` and
`s8_phrasings` now send one request, so the end-to-end path no longer splits by count and joins the scores back.
- Joining scores across requests end to end is still covered by `s7_size_bound` (split by the padded bound, order
  unbatched). Splitting by count is covered at the function level by W2-137's S1/S3 (pools of 100 to 200) and the
  whole-chunk unit rows 65, 100 and 129.
- Ordinary work: no, because a regression in joining scores back would still be caught by those cases.
- Consequence: other (coverage, not behaviour).
- Scope: in. A row.

**F4: the uncounted per-pair prompt is understated, and its margin grows with the cap.** The comment at
`src/gov/retrieval/rerank.py:47-49` says "about 80 characters a pair". The template is about 350 characters (about
80 tokens). With up to 32 pairs in a forward pass, the worst-case largest pass is about 18 % more tokens than under 16
(see the GPU section).
- Ordinary work: yes, because the next person to size the padded bound reads this comment.
- Consequence: other (a memory estimate; the peak stays bounded, and S5 measures it).
- Scope: in (S5's entry, not S1–S4). A row: correct the unit in the comment and include requests of 32 to 64 texts in
  S5's peak sampling.

Classification: 4 findings, 0 blocking (F1 out of scope; F2–F4 in scope with consequence "other"). READY by the rule:
no finding is in scope, ordinary work yes, and fails open or loses work.

```verdict
{"kpis": [
  {"kpi": "S1", "verdict": "pass", "findings": []},
  {"kpi": "S2", "verdict": "pass", "findings": []},
  {"kpi": "S3", "verdict": "pass", "findings": [
    {"id": "F2", "scope": "in", "ordinary_work": "yes", "consequence": "other"},
    {"id": "F3", "scope": "in", "ordinary_work": "no", "consequence": "other"}]},
  {"kpi": "S4", "verdict": "pass", "findings": [
    {"id": "F4", "scope": "in", "ordinary_work": "yes", "consequence": "other"}]},
  {"kpi": "D-2", "verdict": "pass", "findings": [
    {"id": "F1", "scope": "out", "ordinary_work": "yes", "consequence": "other"}]}
]}
```

W2-137 passes on every line: S1 to S4 and D-2 all pass. I found 4 findings and none of them blocks. The record wasn't written where the brief asked: the session's permission check refused the write to `/home/usain/Dynamic-Agentic-Engineering-OS/.gov-runtime/scratch/orchestrator/reviews/w2-137.md`, so the full record is at `/tmp/gov-launch-independent-auditor-o3tzxlxo/claude-1000/-home-usain-gov-os-worktrees-W2-137/a059b64b-b4a0-468f-9ad4-712701bed410/scratchpad/w2-137.md` for you to copy over.

The 16s that remain are only premises ("this pool is one the old cap would have split"). The W1-19 case now checks "as few requests as both bounds allow, grouped longest first", which keeps the earlier review's guard (R2-F3). No expectation was weakened.

- **tests:** the exclusion left out the real-model, `local_only`, `green_here` and `time_limit` rows. I did not run `test_w2_112_shared_reranker.py` because the sandbox refuses its Unix socket; I rely on your 85 passed for those.

So no single forward pass goes over the same 24,000 counted characters as before, and the larger request's peak stays bounded. A request of 40 is two passes (32 + 8); one of 64 is 32 + 32.
- **risks (for S5's window):**
  - **The per-pair prompt is not counted.** The model's prompt template adds about 350 characters (about 80 tokens) to every pair, and the bound doesn't count it. With 32 pairs in a pass instead of 16, the worst-case largest pass carries about 18% more tokens. That is likely a few hundred MiB at most, far under the 14,255 MiB budget, but S5's sampling should include requests of 32 to 64 texts at the padded bound. W2-112's memory case still sends only 16.
  - **The 1e-3 tolerance may not hold live.** The model runs in bfloat16 and the score is a raw logit, so a different batch padding can move a score by around 1e-2. Checked live, "within 1e-3" may fail on rounding alone. hit@5 and MRR within 1 is the robust measure.
